lesson.title: Safer school WhatsApp groups
lesson.subtitle: Settings and habits that protect pupils and staff

video.title: Safer school WhatsApp groups
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Amina at home in the evening, her phone buzzing nonstop on the table. Three notification bubbles stack up: a huge group of tiny faces, a photo of a mark sheet with a blurred grid, and a message from a contact with the head teacher’s photo and a money icon.
scenes.animation: Bubbles stack with small bounces, 300 ms apart. Amina’s eyes widen; quick push-in.
scenes.narration: A huge group I never joined. Our mark sheet posted in the parents’ group. And now the “head teacher” wants airtime? What is going on tonight?
scenes.sound: Rapid notification pings; light music bed starts.
scenes.vids: Character: illustrated primary teacher in a headscarf, ink outlines. Show chats as generic bubbles; never show a real app’s name, logo or layout.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey card. The Darsi mark pops in, then the on-screen title and the cyber track chip with its icon.
scenes.animation: Mark scales 0→100% with a small overshoot (≤ 200 ms); title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: the settings and habits that make school groups safer — for you, your pupils and your colleagues.
scenes.vids: Use the Darsi title template (see brand kit). Keep the chip as icon + word. Keep app names off screen.

scenes.visual: A group chat drawn as a round table of small figures. One figure with a star badge (the admin) flips three switches on a panel: speech bubble, pencil, person with a check. The busy chatter bubbles calm down to a few clear notices.
scenes.animation: Switches flip 300 ms apart; chatter bubbles shrink and fade, leaving two neat notice cards.
scenes.narration: If you’re an admin — a member who can change the group’s settings — start there. In a notice group, let only admins send messages and edit the group’s details. Then turn on approval for new members, so nobody joins by link without a check.
scenes.sound: Three soft switch clicks; chatter fades.
scenes.vids: Draw a generic settings panel with icons only; do not copy any real app’s screens.

scenes.visual: Amina’s own phone. A stranger’s hand tries to pull her into a group and bounces off a contacts-book shield. Then a six-dot PIN box appears with a key, and a figure holding a stolen text code is stopped at a locked door.
scenes.animation: The hand bounces off with a soft boing; PIN dots fill one by one; the door stays shut with a small shake.
scenes.narration: Next, your own account. In privacy settings, choose who can add you to groups — my contacts only stops strangers adding you to scam groups. And turn on two-step verification: a six-digit PIN that the app asks for when your number is set up on a phone.
scenes.sound: Soft boing, then six light taps.
scenes.vids: Show the code holder as a neutral silhouette, not a stereotype. Show the PIN as dots only.

scenes.visual: Clean card with the cyber track chip. A text-code bubble and a six-dot PIN sit side by side; a door opens only when both are placed on it.
scenes.animation: The code bubble slides in and the door stays shut; the PIN slides in and the door swings open. 1.5 s total.
scenes.narration: Two-step verification means a stolen text code isn’t enough. Without your PIN, a scammer can’t move your account to their phone.
scenes.vids: Keep the card on screen for at least 6 seconds so teachers can read it in a second language.

scenes.visual: A school notice board inside the gate. An office worker pins a sports-day notice and a visitor reads it. A hand starts to pin a report card, pauses, and carries it back to the office instead.
scenes.animation: The pin presses in; the report card slides back out of frame.
scenes.narration: Think of the school notice board. Only the office pins notices, and nobody pins a pupil’s report card there for every visitor to read. A school group works the same way.
scenes.vids: Notice board with simple icon notices only; no readable names or marks.

scenes.visual: Mr Joseph Mwangi pops in holding a phone that shows a mark-list photo in a group chat. Two answer cards drop in: a thumbs up (fine to post) and an envelope with one person (share privately).
scenes.animation: Character slides in from the side; answer cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A parent posts the whole class mark list in the parents’ group. Is that OK?
scenes.sound: Two gentle ‘pop’ sounds for the cards.
scenes.vids: The app pauses here (diamond marker). For the MP4 shared outside the app, hold this frame for 3 seconds with a small countdown ring.

scenes.visual: The ‘share privately’ card gets a blue check badge. The mark-list photo shrinks and splits into separate envelopes, each flying to one family’s house.
scenes.animation: Check badge pops (150 ms). Quick 0.8 s confetti of three shapes in kola, sunbird and ink.
scenes.narration: No. Members can usually see each other’s numbers and forward anything in seconds. Pupils’ marks, photos and phone numbers stay out of big groups. If you’re the admin, delete the post and message the parent privately.
scenes.vids: Use blue for correct (never green) and always pair it with the check icon.

scenes.visual: A chat bubble from a contact with the head teacher’s photo shows a money icon and a clock. Amina pauses, opens her saved contacts and calls the head teacher, who answers from her office, surprised, shaking her head.
scenes.animation: The clock icon ticks; a call wave travels to the office; the head teacher shakes her head once.
scenes.narration: Now, that “head teacher”. Anyone can put a name and photo on a new number. “I’m in a meeting — send airtime urgently” is a common trick. Call the head teacher on the number you already have.
scenes.sound: Ticking clock; phone ring; a relieved laugh.
scenes.vids: Show the head teacher as a friendly illustrated figure; the fake contact uses the same photo with a small question mark.

scenes.visual: Amina posts a short warning in the staff group (a bubble with a warning triangle), then opens the fake contact and taps a flag and a block symbol. The fake contact turns grey.
scenes.animation: Warning bubble pops; flag and block icons pop 200 ms apart; the contact fades to grey.
scenes.narration: If it’s a scam, warn the group, then report and block the number: open the chat, tap the name or number, and choose report or block.
scenes.vids: Show generic flag and block icons, not a real app’s menu.

scenes.visual: Amina faces the viewer. Beside her, a colleague’s phone shows a text code being handed to a shadowy figure. Three answer cards bounce in: a group with a star badge, a key with six dots, a muted bell.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Someone tricks a colleague into sharing her six-digit text code. Which setting protects her account?
scenes.vids: Second diamond marker — the app pauses for the question. In the MP4, hold for 3 seconds, then highlight ‘two-step verification PIN’.

scenes.visual: The PIN card gets the check badge. Then four summary cards line up: a star-badged figure with switches, a key with six dots, a crossed-out photo, a phone calling a saved contact.
scenes.animation: Cards line up left to right, 250 ms apart.
scenes.narration: Two-step verification — yes. Remember: admins control the group, a PIN protects your account, pupils’ details stay out, and urgent requests get a phone call.
scenes.vids: Hold the four cards for 5 seconds.

scenes.visual: Amina’s classroom. A phone with an empty group chat is drawn on the board. Pupils call out rules; Amina writes five of them in chalk, and pupils sign the poster below. End card: Darsi mark and ‘Next unit: Accounts and devices’.
scenes.animation: Rules appear one by one in chalk; signatures pop on. End card fades in.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: ask pupils to design the rules for a class group — who posts, what is never shared, and what to do with a strange message.
scenes.sound: Music resolves; no end jingle longer than 1 s.
scenes.vids: Classroom: illustrated pupils in local school uniforms; avoid stereotyped imagery. End card from the Darsi template.

checkpoints.prompt: A parent posts the whole class mark list in the parents’ group. Is that OK?

options.text: No — marks are shared one to one or on paper

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — members can save and forward anything. Each family should see only their own child’s marks.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — every family would see every child’s marks, and anyone can forward them. Share marks one to one.

checkpoints.prompt: Someone tricks a colleague into sharing her six-digit text code. Which setting protects her account?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — without her PIN, the code alone isn’t enough to set up her account on another phone.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — group settings and muting don’t protect her account. A two-step verification PIN does.

video.vids_prompt: Create a 3 minute animated explainer video for teachers about safer school WhatsApp groups; the on-screen title is “Safer school chat groups”. Style: flat, friendly illustration with ink outlines, light grey backgrounds, a tangerine (#ff6a2b) brand colour and hibiscus pink (#f04a7e); no gradients or blur. Main character: Amina, a primary school teacher. Follow the script scene by scene: an evening of group problems; admin settings; who can add you and a two-step PIN; the notice-board analogy; keeping pupils’ marks and photos out; a fake “head teacher” asking for airtime; warn, report and block; two quiz pauses; end with pupils writing class group rules. Use the narration exactly as written, a warm, calm voice, and keep on-screen text to six words or fewer per scene. Never show app names, logos or app screens.
